enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1135 AM MDT Sat Oct 24 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 1103 AM MDT Sat Oct 24 2026

 - Widespread showers and thunderstorms again going into this evening.
   Best chances for areas east of the Rio Grande, including El 
   Paso, Hudspeth, and Otero Counties. Storms will be capable of 
   large hail, damaging winds, and localized flash flooding.

 - Storm chances shift further east Sunday and Monday, limited
   mostly to Hudspeth and Otero Counties. A brief window of drier
   weather expected midweek before rain chances return Thursday
   into next weekend.

 - Typical late-October temperatures, with lowland highs in the
   lower to mid 70s.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1103 AM MDT Sat Oct 24 2026

Another active late afternoon and evening expected with an almost
exact same pattern as yesterday. The main difference is that the
moisture will be move out of western zones and the focus will be
the RGV east. Shear and instability remain in place, so initial
cells will be capable of producing large hail and damaging winds.
Good agreement among CAMs that storms will congeal into a bow type
echo as it heads east out of the area. The NBM PoPs seemed too
high over the west and tapered back some. 

For Sun, upper low that will be bringing us the weather today 
will be lifting NE into UT/CO border region and drier air will 
continue a eastward push. Again, models agree that the drier air 
makes it into the RGV and possibly as far east as the Hudspeth 
county line. There will remain shear and decent instability over 
far eastern zones, so a few at least marginally severe storms are 
possible. Areas to the west will see west to southwest winds and 
should be able to warm up nicely into the 70s to lower 80s. Monday
the models are differing on a westward push of moisture/cooler
air. The GFS continues to be the odd model out and keeps moisture
east while others bring it at least through the Continental
Divide. AIGFS is also looking closer to EC/NAM so will go that way
which mainly affects temps. Slightly cooler then for Mon,
especially eastern zones. Will also keep shower/thunderstorm
chances going out there and again, a few severe are not out of the
question.  

A westerly flow gradually pushes moisture and instability east of
the area for Tue/Wed. Not much chance if any for precipitation and
temperatures will be the warmest of the forecast period.  

Another storm system moves into the West Coast for the end of the
week with southwest flow tapping some more sub-tropical moisture
and rain chances return. Could be some good rainfall amounts for
Thu/Fri. Models showing some shear over the area but instability
isn't as high as recent days. Temperatures will start cooling 
down with increased cloud cover and moisture. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1103 AM MDT Sat Oct 24 2026

P6SM FEW-BKN060-080 to start the period with a few isolated
showers and thunderstorms in area mountains. By 20Z, expect to
have scattered to nmrs VRB20G35KT 1-3SM TSRA BKN040-060 developing
mainly along and east of the RGV. Some storms will be severe again
with large hail and damaging winds. Storms push east of the area
by 06Z with skies over the west becoming SKC-FEW120 while the
eastern areas will be SCT-BKN060-080 BKN200-250. Winds south to
southeast 5-15G25KTS turning more west to southwest on the west
side of the Divide through the afternoon.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1103 AM MDT Sat Oct 24 2026

Continue on with the fire threat being low as we will remain in a
fairly active pattern bringing showers and thunderstorms from time
to time. For the next few days, this precip will remain focused
east of the RGV. A couple days of drier weather then a return to a
more moist pattern. Temperatures will remain at or above normal
with RH's at or above 20%. Vent rates will be good Sun and drop to
poor to fair for Mon. 

&&
